instructions: Rinse the rice in a strainer under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave the lid on until you're ready to serve.
Wash the chives and dry them well. Cut them into 1/2 inch pieces. That should be about 3 cups.
In a small bowl, stir 2 tsp cornstarch into 1 1/2 tbsp cold water until smooth.
Crack the 8 eggs into a large bowl. Add the sugar, salt, white pepper, sesame oil and 2 tbsp water. Beat for 30 seconds, until small bubbles form on top.
Stir the cornstarch mixture again, then stir it into the eggs. Mix in the chives.
Heat a wok or 12 inch nonstick skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke, then turn the heat to medium-low. Wait 10 seconds, add 3 tbsp of the vegetable oil and swirl it around.

Stir the egg mixture, then pour half of it into the pan. Stir and flip it slowly with a spatula for about 2 minutes, until the eggs are just set and still glossy. Don't let them brown. Transfer them to a plate.
Wipe the pan, heat the last 3 tbsp oil and cook the rest of the egg mixture the same way.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: The Woks of Life version leads (5.0 from 26 ratings): eggs beaten with salt, a pinch of sugar, white pepper and sesame oil, a little cornstarch slurry for a tender curd, then chives folded in and cooked fast in a wok. Other versions on the first page of results agree that salt and chives carry the dish. The lead's Shaoxing wine is left out to keep it gluten-free, and the amounts are scaled from 5 eggs to 8, cooked in two batches so the eggs stay soft.
